notice: A typical topic progression for orientation only; not a binding curriculum mapping for any German state.

subtopics.label: Numbers on the number line
subtopics.learning_goal: Place whole numbers on a number line and compare them by their position.
misconceptions: The marks are read as unequally spaced, so the scale is misjudged.
A number further to the left is called larger because its digits are larger.

subtopics.label: Understanding negative numbers
subtopics.learning_goal: Read and order negative numbers and explain what they mean below zero.
misconceptions: Minus 7 is treated as larger than minus 3 because 7 is larger than 3.
The minus sign is read as a subtraction instead of as part of the number.

subtopics.label: Comparing and ordering numbers
subtopics.learning_goal: Order a set of integers and justify each comparison using the number line.
misconceptions: Numbers are compared digit by digit regardless of how many digits they have.
The symbols for less than and greater than are read in the wrong direction.

subtopics.label: Order of operations
subtopics.learning_goal: Apply multiplication before addition and use brackets to change the order on purpose.
misconceptions: The expression is evaluated strictly from left to right.
Brackets are dropped without adjusting the operation that remains.

subtopics.label: Divisibility rules
subtopics.learning_goal: Decide whether a number is divisible by 2, 3, 5 or 10 without carrying out the division.
misconceptions: The rule for 3 is applied to the last digit instead of to the digit sum.
Divisibility by 2 and divisibility by 4 are treated as the same test.

subtopics.label: Prime factors
subtopics.learning_goal: Write a natural number as a product of prime factors and explain why that product is unique.
misconceptions: The number 1 is included as a prime factor.
The factor tree is stopped before every branch has reached a prime.

subtopics.label: Recognising and measuring angles
subtopics.learning_goal: Measure an angle with a protractor and classify it as acute, right or obtuse.
misconceptions: The outer scale of the protractor is read instead of the inner one.
The angle is judged by the drawn length of its arms rather than by its opening.

subtopics.label: Points in the coordinate system
subtopics.learning_goal: Plot and read points in the coordinate system using ordered pairs.
misconceptions: The first and second coordinate are swapped when plotting.
Counting starts at the first grid line instead of at the origin.

subtopics.label: Axis symmetry
subtopics.learning_goal: Find the axis of symmetry of a figure and construct the mirror image of a point.
misconceptions: The mirror image is drawn at an unequal distance from the axis.
A figure is called symmetric although its halves do not match when folded.

subtopics.label: Converting units
subtopics.learning_goal: Convert between metric units of length, mass and time using the place value structure.
misconceptions: The decimal point is moved by one place instead of by the conversion factor.
Area units are converted with the same factor as length units.

subtopics.label: Area and perimeter of the rectangle
subtopics.learning_goal: Distinguish perimeter from area and calculate both for a rectangle.
misconceptions: Perimeter and area are used interchangeably.
The area is reported in centimetres instead of in square centimetres.

subtopics.label: Areas of composite figures
subtopics.learning_goal: Split a composite figure into rectangles and add or subtract their areas.
misconceptions: An overlapping part is counted twice.
A missing side length is guessed instead of derived from the other sides.

subtopics.label: Expanding and reducing fractions
subtopics.learning_goal: Expand and reduce a fraction and explain why its value does not change.
misconceptions: Only the numerator is multiplied when the fraction is expanded.
A fraction is reduced by subtracting the same number from numerator and denominator.

subtopics.label: Adding fractions
subtopics.learning_goal: Add fractions with different denominators by using a common denominator.
misconceptions: Numerators and denominators are added separately.
A common denominator is found but the numerators are not adjusted with it.

subtopics.label: Multiplying and dividing fractions
subtopics.learning_goal: Multiply fractions directly and divide by multiplying with the reciprocal.
misconceptions: A common denominator is created before multiplying.
Multiplication is expected to always make the result larger.

subtopics.label: Place value in decimals
subtopics.learning_goal: Read the place value of each digit after the decimal point and compare decimals.
misconceptions: 0.7 is treated as smaller than 0.25 because 25 is larger than 7.
Trailing zeros are believed to change the value.

subtopics.label: Calculating with decimals
subtopics.learning_goal: Add, subtract and multiply decimals and place the decimal point correctly.
misconceptions: Digits are aligned at the right edge instead of at the decimal point.
The number of decimal places in a product is taken from one factor only.

subtopics.label: Fractions and decimals
subtopics.learning_goal: Convert between fractions and decimals and recognise a repeating decimal.
misconceptions: The fraction bar is read as a decimal point, so one quarter becomes 1.4.
Every fraction is expected to give a terminating decimal.

subtopics.label: Understanding the percentage value
subtopics.learning_goal: Identify base value, percentage rate and percentage value and calculate the percentage value.
misconceptions: The percentage value is confused with the base value.
A percentage increase is applied by appending the rate to the number.

subtopics.label: Proportional relationships
subtopics.learning_goal: Recognise a proportional relationship from a table or a graph and use its constant ratio.
misconceptions: Any relationship that increases is treated as proportional.
The graph is not expected to pass through the origin.

subtopics.label: The rule of three
subtopics.learning_goal: Solve a proportional problem by reducing to one unit and then scaling up.
misconceptions: The rule of three is applied to an inversely proportional situation.
The step to one unit is skipped, so the scaling factor is wrong.

subtopics.label: Angles at intersecting lines
subtopics.learning_goal: Use vertical and supplementary angles to find unknown angles at intersecting lines.
misconceptions: Vertical angles and adjacent angles are mixed up.
Angles are assumed to be equal because they look similar in the drawing.

subtopics.label: Area of the triangle
subtopics.learning_goal: Calculate the area of a triangle and explain where the factor one half comes from.
misconceptions: The factor one half is forgotten.
A slanted side is used as the height instead of the perpendicular height.

subtopics.label: Area of parallelogram and trapezium
subtopics.learning_goal: Calculate the area of a parallelogram and a trapezium using the perpendicular height.
misconceptions: The slanted side is used instead of the perpendicular height.
For the trapezium only one of the two parallel sides is used.

subtopics.label: Simplifying expressions
subtopics.learning_goal: Collect like terms and explain why unlike terms cannot be combined.
misconceptions: Terms with different variables are added together.
The sign in front of a term is dropped when the term is moved.

subtopics.label: Solving linear equations
subtopics.learning_goal: Solve a linear equation by applying the same operation to both sides.
misconceptions: The operation is applied to one side of the equation only.
Dividing by a negative number leaves the sign unchanged.

subtopics.label: Expanding and factorising
subtopics.learning_goal: Expand a product over a sum and reverse the step by factoring out a common factor.
misconceptions: Only the first term inside the bracket is multiplied.
A minus in front of a bracket is not applied to every term inside it.

subtopics.label: Mean and median
subtopics.learning_goal: Calculate mean and median and say which of the two an outlier distorts.
misconceptions: The median is read off without ordering the data first.
Mean and median are expected to always coincide.

subtopics.label: Constructing triangles
subtopics.learning_goal: Construct a triangle from given sides and angles with compass and straight edge.
misconceptions: The compass width is changed between two arcs.
Any three given values are assumed to determine one triangle.

subtopics.label: Congruence theorems
subtopics.learning_goal: Use the congruence theorems to decide whether two triangles are congruent.
misconceptions: Equal angles alone are taken as proof of congruence.
The angle used is not the one enclosed by the two given sides.

subtopics.label: Angle sum in the triangle
subtopics.learning_goal: Use the 180 degree angle sum to find a missing angle in a triangle.
misconceptions: The angle sum of a quadrilateral is used for a triangle.
An exterior angle is added to the interior angles.

subtopics.label: Angles at parallel lines
subtopics.learning_goal: Identify corresponding and alternate angles at parallel lines cut by a transversal.
misconceptions: Corresponding angles and alternate angles are confused.
The rules are applied although the two lines are not parallel.

subtopics.label: The exterior angle
subtopics.learning_goal: Relate an exterior angle to the two non adjacent interior angles.
misconceptions: The exterior angle is set equal to the adjacent interior angle.
All three interior angles are added instead of only two.

subtopics.label: Direct proportion
subtopics.learning_goal: Recognise direct proportion and use its constant quotient.
misconceptions: The graph is not expected to pass through the origin.
Adding a constant is confused with multiplying by a factor.

subtopics.label: Inverse proportion
subtopics.learning_goal: Recognise inverse proportion and use its constant product.
misconceptions: Inverse proportion is handled with the constant quotient rule.
The graph is drawn as a straight line.

subtopics.label: Proportion in applications
subtopics.learning_goal: Decide from the context whether a relationship is directly or inversely proportional.
misconceptions: Every relationship in a word problem is assumed to be proportional.
Doubling one quantity is assumed to double the other.

subtopics.label: Understanding slope
subtopics.learning_goal: Explain and calculate slope as the ratio of the change in height to the change across.
misconceptions: The numerator and denominator of dy/dx are swapped.
Slope is read off a single point instead of between two points.

subtopics.label: Line equation y = mx + b
subtopics.learning_goal: Read slope and y-intercept from a line equation and sketch the matching graph.
misconceptions: The roles of m and b are swapped when reading the equation.
The value of b is read as an x-value instead of as the y-intercept.

subtopics.label: Zero and axis intercepts
subtopics.learning_goal: Find the zero of a linear function and mark both axis intercepts on the graph.
misconceptions: The zero of the function is read off the y-axis.
Setting y to zero and setting x to zero are interchanged.

subtopics.label: Systems of linear equations
subtopics.learning_goal: Solve a system of two linear equations and interpret the solution as a point of intersection.
misconceptions: The substitution is put back into the same equation it came from.
A system without a solution is reported as x equals zero.

subtopics.label: Laplace experiments
subtopics.learning_goal: Calculate a probability as favourable outcomes divided by equally likely outcomes.
misconceptions: Outcomes that are not equally likely are treated as a Laplace experiment.
A probability is given as a number greater than one.

subtopics.label: Tree diagrams
subtopics.learning_goal: Use a tree diagram to find the probability of a two stage experiment.
misconceptions: Probabilities along one path are added instead of multiplied.
The branch probabilities leaving one node do not add up to one.

subtopics.label: Circumference of the circle
subtopics.learning_goal: Relate circumference and diameter through pi and calculate the circumference.
misconceptions: The radius is used where the diameter is required.
Pi is treated as exactly 3.14 rather than as an approximation.

subtopics.label: Area of the circle
subtopics.learning_goal: Calculate the area of a circle and distinguish it clearly from the circumference.
misconceptions: The formulas for area and circumference are swapped.
The radius is not squared.

subtopics.label: Sectors and arcs
subtopics.learning_goal: Calculate arc length and sector area as a fraction of the whole circle.
misconceptions: The central angle is not related to the full 360 degrees.
Arc length is calculated with the area formula.

subtopics.label: The binomial formulas
subtopics.learning_goal: Apply the three binomial formulas to expand and to factorise.
misconceptions: The middle term with the factor two is omitted.
A squared difference is expanded as a difference of squares.

subtopics.label: Simplifying fraction terms
subtopics.learning_goal: Reduce a fraction term by factorising first and state the excluded values.
misconceptions: A summand is cancelled instead of a factor.
The values that make the denominator zero are not excluded.

subtopics.label: Equations with fraction terms
subtopics.learning_goal: Solve an equation containing fractions by multiplying with the common denominator.
misconceptions: Only one term is multiplied by the common denominator.
A solution that makes a denominator zero is accepted.

topics.label: Square roots and the Pythagorean theorem

subtopics.label: Understanding square roots
subtopics.learning_goal: Read a square root as the side length of a square and estimate it between two whole numbers.
misconceptions: The square root is treated as half of the number.
A negative number is given a real square root.

subtopics.label: The Pythagorean theorem
subtopics.learning_goal: Use the Pythagorean theorem to find a missing side in a right angled triangle.
misconceptions: The hypotenuse is not identified as the side opposite the right angle.
The squares are added but the root is never taken.

subtopics.label: Rational and irrational numbers
subtopics.learning_goal: Distinguish rational from irrational numbers and place both on the number line.
misconceptions: Every square root is assumed to be irrational.
A repeating decimal is classified as irrational.

subtopics.label: Quadratic functions
subtopics.learning_goal: Describe how the coefficients shape the parabola and locate its vertex.
misconceptions: A plus inside the bracket is read as a shift to the right.
A negative leading coefficient is thought to move the parabola down rather than to open it downward.

subtopics.label: Similarity and the intercept theorem
subtopics.learning_goal: Use the intercept theorem to find a missing length between similar figures.
misconceptions: Corresponding sides are paired incorrectly.
Differences of lengths are compared instead of ratios.

subtopics.label: Solving quadratic equations
subtopics.learning_goal: Solve a quadratic equation and use the discriminant to say how many solutions exist.
misconceptions: Only the positive root is reported.
The equation is not brought into standard form before the formula is applied.

subtopics.label: Volume of the prism
subtopics.learning_goal: Calculate the volume of a prism as base area times height.
misconceptions: A slanted edge is used as the height.
The volume is reported in square units.

subtopics.label: Volume of the pyramid
subtopics.learning_goal: Calculate the volume of a pyramid and explain where the factor one third comes from.
misconceptions: The factor one third is forgotten.
The slant height is used instead of the perpendicular height.

subtopics.label: Surface area of solids
subtopics.learning_goal: Find the surface area of a prism or a pyramid from its net.
misconceptions: A face is counted twice or left out entirely.
The volume formula is used where the surface area is asked for.

subtopics.label: Relative frequency
subtopics.learning_goal: Distinguish relative frequency from probability and describe what happens over many trials.
misconceptions: A short run of trials is expected to match the probability exactly.
Past outcomes are believed to influence the next one.

subtopics.label: Counting outcomes
subtopics.learning_goal: Count the outcomes of a multi stage experiment with the product rule.
misconceptions: Outcomes of the stages are added instead of multiplied.
Order is ignored in a situation where it matters.

subtopics.label: Box plots and spread
subtopics.learning_goal: Read median, quartiles and range from a box plot.
misconceptions: The box is read as containing all of the data.
A wider box is read as a higher average.

subtopics.label: Exponential growth
subtopics.learning_goal: Describe exponential growth by its constant growth factor and contrast it with linear growth.
misconceptions: A constant difference is used where a constant factor is required.
A growth of five percent is modelled by adding five each step.

subtopics.label: Understanding logarithms
subtopics.learning_goal: Read a logarithm as the exponent that produces a given value and solve a simple exponential equation.
misconceptions: The logarithm of a sum is split into a sum of logarithms.
The base of the logarithm is ignored.

subtopics.label: Graphs of exponential functions
subtopics.learning_goal: Describe how the base and a factor change the graph of an exponential function.
misconceptions: The graph is expected to cross the x-axis.
A base between zero and one is not recognised as decay.

subtopics.label: Sine and cosine
subtopics.learning_goal: Define sine and cosine as ratios in the right angled triangle and find a missing side with them.
misconceptions: The opposite and the adjacent side are swapped.
The calculator is left in the wrong angle mode.

subtopics.label: Cone and sphere
subtopics.learning_goal: Calculate volume and surface area of a cone and of a sphere.
misconceptions: The slant height is used as the height in the volume formula.
The factor one third is applied to the sphere as well.

subtopics.label: The tangent ratio
subtopics.learning_goal: Use the tangent ratio to find an angle or a side in a right angled triangle.
misconceptions: The tangent ratio is applied to the hypotenuse.
The inverse function is not used when the angle is the unknown.

subtopics.label: The sine function
subtopics.learning_goal: Describe period and amplitude of the sine function and read both from its graph.
misconceptions: Amplitude and period are confused.
The graph is expected to stop after one period.

subtopics.label: Sine rule and cosine rule
subtopics.learning_goal: Choose between the sine rule and the cosine rule for a triangle without a right angle.
misconceptions: The Pythagorean theorem is applied to a triangle without a right angle.
The second possible angle in the sine rule is overlooked.

subtopics.label: The unit circle
subtopics.learning_goal: Read sine and cosine of an angle as coordinates of a point on the unit circle.
misconceptions: Sine and cosine are read on the wrong axis.
Angles beyond 90 degrees are treated as undefined.

subtopics.label: Power functions
subtopics.learning_goal: Compare the graphs of power functions with even and with odd exponents.
misconceptions: A negative exponent is read as a negative function value.
Every power function is expected to pass through the origin.

subtopics.label: Shifting and stretching graphs
subtopics.learning_goal: Predict how adding or multiplying a constant shifts or stretches a graph.
misconceptions: A plus inside the function argument is read as a shift to the right.
A factor in front of the function is thought to shift the graph vertically.

subtopics.label: The hyperbola
subtopics.learning_goal: Describe the graph of the reciprocal function and its behaviour near the axes.
misconceptions: The graph is expected to touch the axes.
The two branches are joined into one curve through zero.
